run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Evidence from Loki, Kubernetes object state and events shows that the payment-api application in namespace app-101 (container/pod label payment-api-101-8486559b69-5tqhv, service label payment-api) failed repeatedly between 13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z on 2026-11-20 with the exact message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted", reporting wait_time_ms from 1227 to 4840 and queue_length from 5 to 15. In the log windows sampled before that (05:01–13:42Z) every returned line was a successful "Payment processed successfully" INFO line, and after 14:44Z the sampled lines return to successful payments (14:49Z, 15:27Z and later, plus "Payment API started" at 2026-11-21T04:59:29Z), so the failure burst is bounded by the sampled log lines to roughly 13:46–14:44 on Nov 20. The error names the payment-api process's own database connection pool as the failing resource; the database itself is not visible: the cluster service list contains no database service and Loki holds only the payment-api stream family, so the dependency that exhausted the pool could not be identified. The payment-api-101 Deployment/Pod objects no longer existed at query time (only loki existed in app-101), so the pod spec, pool settings, restart history and pod-level status at 13:45Z could not be read. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) for every attempt, so error rate, latency baseline, traces and pod metrics are unknown. The failure and its exact error text are established; the object or configuration that caused the pool exhaustion is not, so the root cause is left null.

claims.text: The Loki query for namespace app-101 over 2026-11-20T13:40:00Z–14:50:00Z returned 8 lines, all level ERROR with message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted", service payment-api, pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-5tqhv, timestamps 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z, 13:54:00Z, 14:03:00Z, 14:15:00Z, 14:19:00Z, 14:21:00Z, 14:31:00Z and 14:44:00Z, each carrying wait_time_ms 1227, 2104, 1495, 2965, 4005, 4840, 2358, 3836 and queue_length 10, 11, 8, 9, 10, 8, 15, 5 respectively.

In the sampled log window before the burst (2026-11-20T05:01:00Z–13:42:00Z) the Loki query returned 10 lines, all level INFO "Payment processed successfully" (05:04Z through 12:57Z, plus 11:19Z, 11:40Z, 11:44Z, 06:00Z, 06:34Z, 06:40Z, 05:27Z, 05:50Z), with lines_shown 10 and lines_omitted 0; no ERROR line appears among the returned lines.

In the sampled log window after the burst (2026-11-20T15:28:00Z–2026-11-21T05:01:00Z) the Loki query returned 14 lines, all level INFO, consisting of "Payment processed successfully" entries (17:01Z through 03:54Z) and one "Payment API started" line at 2026-11-21T04:59:29.441857Z with port 8080; no ERROR line appears among them.

Successful INFO payments interleave with the error burst: 2026-11-20T13:42:00Z (PAY-5032), 13:59:00Z (PAY-1800) and 14:49:00Z (PAY-8206) were logged between the failure lines, and 15:27:00Z (PAY-4120) followed them.

A Loki metric query over 2026-11-20T13:40:00Z–13:50:00Z with selector {job=~".+"} returned exactly one series, job=payment-api and namespace=app-101, i.e. no other log stream family was returned for that window.

At 2026-11-21T05:01:03Z the namespace app-101 contained only one pod, loki-66445c6d6f-n9d4s (Running, 0 restarts, owned by ReplicaSet loki-66445c6d6f); no payment-api pod was present, and the cluster-wide pod listing returned 33 pods with none in app-101 other than that loki pod.

The deployment listing at 2026-11-21T05:01:06Z returned 25 Deployments, of which the only one in app-101 was loki (1/1 ready); no Deployment named payment-api-101 was in the returned list, and the app-101 ReplicaSet listing returned only loki-66445c6d6f.

The cluster service listing returned 30 Services; in app-101 the only Service was loki (ClusterIP, port 3100) and no database Service appeared in any namespace, so no in-cluster database endpoint for payment-api is visible.

The events returned for app-101 all carry timestamps on 2026-11-21 between 04:59:05Z and 04:59:41Z, i.e. none covers 2026-11-20T13:45Z; they include Deployment payment-api-101 "Scaled up replica set payment-api-101-8486559b69 from 0 to 1" at 04:59:28Z, the pod being scheduled, image python:3.9-slim pulled, containers created/started at 04:59:29Z, and Killing "Stopping container payment-api" and "Stopping container promtail" at 04:59:41Z.

The app-101 ConfigMaps hold only kube-root-ca.crt, loki-config and promtail-config; promtail-config defines the scraper job payment-api with namespace app-101 and path /var/log/*.log, and neither ConfigMap contains any database or connection-pool setting for payment-api.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo defines fault-injection style flags including paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable"), each state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off" as read at 2026-11-21T05:02:38Z.

The alerting_rules.yml stored in the otel-demo prometheus ConfigMap defines the groups opspilot-lab (alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh on checkout PlaceOrder server error ratio in namespace otel-demo) and opspilot-self (OpsPilotAgentAbsent, OpsPilotModelCallsFailing); it contains no alert on app-101 or payment-api.

The proximate cause of the payment failures is exhaustion of payment-api's own database connection pool: the application's own error text says "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" and reports queue_length up to 15 with acquisition waits up to 4840 ms, which fits a saturated pool whose borrowers are not being released fast enough; the pool size and the database behind it are unknown because the payment-api pod/deployment and any DB endpoint are not visible.

A demand or downstream-database slowness spike rather than a code change could have driven the pool exhaustion, since the reported wait_time_ms and queue_length vary per event (1227–4840 ms, 5–15 waiters) and successful payments still completed at 13:59Z during the burst; this cannot be tested because no request-rate, latency or DB metrics are available for the period.

A configuration change to payment-api's pool size or database endpoint could also explain the sudden onset at 13:46Z, but the pod spec, environment variables and any Secret holding the DB DSN/pool size could not be read (the deployment/pod no longer exists and secrets cannot be read), so this remains unverified.

The failure was intermittent, not a full outage: 13:42Z, 13:59Z and 14:49Z show "Payment processed successfully" lines in the same log stream that carries the 13:46Z–14:44Z errors, so not every payment request failed during the burst.

Fault injection through the otel-demo flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable flags is not supported as the cause of the app-101 payment-api pool errors: both flags' value in effect is "off" (defaultVariant off), they belong to the otel-demo flagd ConfigMap and nothing shows the app-101 payment-api consuming flagd; their runtime value on 2026-11-20 remains unknown.

The payment-api-101 pod creation and Killing events at 2026-11-21T04:59:28–04:59:41Z did not cause the Nov 20 13:45Z errors: those events occurred about 15 hours later and are the only payment-api events returned, so they cannot explain the earlier error burst.

Human follow-up: inspect the payment-api application's DB pool size (max connections / acquire timeout) and the database server's max_connections and load for 2026-11-20T13:40Z–14:50Z, since the pool settings and the database identity could not be read from the cluster.

Human follow-up: once the Prometheus and Jaeger sources are reachable, compute payment-api error-rate and latency baselines around 13:45Z and check for DB-side saturation to test the demand/slowness hypothesis instead of relying on the sparse application log lines.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every attempt in this Run (get_metric_names, get_metric_labels-series, metrics_range_query for up, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error rate, request rate, latency baseline, pod resource metrics and kube-state-metrics history (including pod restart/termination reasons for payment-api) are unknown rather than zero.

Jaeger was unavailable for every attempt in this Run (traces_search, traces_list_services, traces_list_operations returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so trace evidence for the payment-api failures and any client-side failures is unknown.

Kubernetes events returned for the authorized window only carried timestamps from 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z to 04:59:41Z; no event covers 2026-11-20T13:45Z, so the kubelet/controller view of the payment-api pod at the incident time is unknown.

The payment-api-101 Deployment and its pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-5tqhv no longer existed at query time (app-101 held only loki), so pod phase, container last termination reason/exit code, restart count, resource limits, environment variables and pool configuration at 13:45Z could not be read.

The database that payment-api connects to is not identifiable: no database Service or workload is visible in the cluster and Loki returned only the payment-api stream family, so the dependency's health and configuration are unknown.
Pool/DB settings could not be verified: app-101 ConfigMaps hold only kube-root-ca.crt, loki-config and promtail-config, and Secrets cannot be read, so any DB_POOL_SIZE / DSN value is unverified.

The cause of the 2026-11-21T04:59Z payment-api-101 scale-up (0 to 1) and the pod's Killing 13 seconds later is unknown; the pod's restart count was 0 and the events are outside the incident time, so this change cannot be placed as impact or as a change for another reason.

Log coverage is sparse (about 36 lines across the whole 24-hour window, roughly one line every several minutes), so the true first/last failure, the number of failed payments and the error rate during 13:45–14:45Z are unknown; the observed 8 error lines are a sample of what Loki held, not a count of failed requests.

networkpolicies and resourcequotas queries returned no objects (status no_data, not citable), so whether network policy or quota played a role in the database connectivity failure could not be established.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
